newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Holding, nervous of more falls.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Holding, nervous of more falls.

text.p: Singapore paper quotes late Tuesday hovered around its morning quotes with the market jittery on further price tumbles, brokers said.
"The market is probably in a very cautious mood at the moment, assessing if cash trades will crash support at $24.00 later today," a broker said.
Prompt physical gas oil has not traded below $24.00 per barrel since July last year.
Some traders were skeptical that the market would test that support, citing slow but gradual demand from China.
They also said the price plunge on Monday has shut the arbitrage window from the west, capping any further supplies sailing east.
But one trader assessed cash market support to move lower than $23.00 a barrel.
"The tanks are full, there is no lack of oil," said one western trader.
Traders said majors suffering from brimming inventories were offering down the market.
July gas oil swaps were last traded at $23.45 per barrel, up from Monday's trade at $23.00.
But traders said the downward potential on both cash and swaps prices is greater than any upward recovery.
"Most traders long on supplies, are buying paper to cover their positions," said one trader, citing the active trade seen Monday.
Brokers said July jet/gas oil regrade was quoted at plus $0.20/0.35, from Monday's indications at $0.10/0.20 cents.
Traders attributed the widening regrade quotes to the weakness in the gas oil market.
Fuel oil swaps hovered around its morning quotes. July was last traded at $98.25 with bids/offers at at $98.00/$98.50.
